messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — I uploaded token-level profiles from the 00:30 canary run to the perf bucket. Seeing a sharp tail in token-latency for /chat/completions when requests hit a KV-cache miss and the runtime falls back to a generic kernel. Pool redwood-dedicated-3 headroom dropped to ~8% around the same time. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/perf?panel=token_breakdown :eyes:

Jordan Li: Link looks useful, thanks. Can you paste the top-line numbers here? Is this a regression after last night's deploy?

Maya Chen: top-line from the canary sample (avg of 30s window): p50=11.6ms, p95=270ms, p99=590ms, token-rate down ~18% compared to baseline. KV-cache-hit-rate for route /chat/completions dropped from 92% -> 64% during spike. Noticed kernel selection logs show fallback on seq_len >= 1024 in several calls.

Kevin Patel: I pulled the profiler traces, looks like kernel selection hit an alignment edgecase and fell back to the generic matmul kernel for some attention spans. Small excerpt from the trace: ```
{
  "request_id": "canary-1769975310-7f2",
  "seq_len": 2048,
  "kernel": "generic_matmul_v1",
  "latency_ms": 620,
  "kv_cache_hit": false
}
```
That fallback accounts for the p99s. Also seeing ~14 cache evictions/min on pool nodes at the time.

Sophie Ramos: Ops saw noisy-neighbor alerts on gpu-7 in redwood-dedicated-3 at ~00:28 — there was a burst of large-batched jobs from a tenant. I think the burst caused KV cache churn + increased batch sizes, which pushed more requests into the fallback kernel path. I added a quick grafana panel: `tokens_by_pod` and a heatmap for batch_size distribution. Query I used: `sum(rate(tokens_generated[1m])) by (pod)`

Jordan Li: For dashboards we should add: 1) token-level latency breakdown by kernel variant (fused vs generic) 2) per-route kv-cache-hit-rate + tokens/sec 3) per-pool headroom + noisy-neighbor score. Also an alert: `pool_headroom_low` if headroom < 10% for 5m. This would have caught the redwood-dedicated-3 event earlier.

Maya Chen: Agreed. I'll open a tiny PR to add those three panels and the alert. Short-term mitigation: rolling backing the kernel alignment change on canary prevents the fallback, so I'm scheduling a rollback now.

Kevin Patel: I'll dig into the alignment check — looks like the optimized kernel's stride calc returns false positives for seq_len multiples of 64 after the change. If we can make selection deterministic based on model dims + quantization flags we avoid runtime fallbacks.

Sophie Ramos: I'll keep an eye on pool headroom and set a 95th-percentile noisy-neighbor alert on pods that show sudden tokens/sec deltas > 3x baseline.

Maya Chen: perf-bot — can you annotate the canary run and create a perf regression issue if the p95/p99 moved by >25% vs baseline? :mag:

perf-bot: Annotated run 1769975310 with tag `kernel-fallback`. Created perf regression issue #3827: "Canary p95/p99 spike due to kernel fallback + KV-cache churn" and linked traces.

oncall-bot: Pager suppressed for this run. Created incident channel #inc-3827 and added oncall for eng-runtime.

Jordan Li: Action items: Maya -> add panels + alert PR; Kevin -> debug alignment/kernel selection; Sophie -> tune noisy-neighbor alert and watch headroom; I'll coordinate with Platform to schedule a capacity buffer for redwood-dedicated-3 until autoscale/burst config is reviewed.

Maya Chen: Thanks — if anyone finds a reproducer for the cache-eviction pattern please drop it here. I'll follow up with the PR link in this thread. :thumbsup:
